Windows Explorer:

braille now also shows the detail columns (date modified, type, size, ...) for the focused file/folder
The NVDA settings allow you to specify whether the language should also read the entire line aloud.
the inline rename edit box (F2) now uses a "Rename" label instead of repeating the file/folder name

If a Markdown file (*.md) is selected in Windows Explorer or total Commander:

NVDA+Alt+Space, Views the file in the NVDA browser.
NVDA+Alt+Shift+Space, saves the file in HTML format.

In all browsers:

NVDA+Ctrl+f4, show page URL, press twice, copy to clipboard.

Generally:

NVDA+Shift+v, shows program name, 32/64bit, CPU usagee, version, product name

Microsoft Outlook 13 or later:

Shift+Alt+j, Jumps to the next folder with unread emails below the Inbox folder.
Shift+Ctrl+Alt+i, Saves the current folder as Folder 1
Shift+Alt+i, Go to Folder 1

A further 4 folders can be defined and jumped to. The folders can also be in another account. Fewer pages that go quiet after finding the right paragraph. Some pages rebuild themselves while the add-on is still reading them, which moves the paragraph it had settled on. It handles that by searching for the paragraph again by its wording, and that search was fussier than the check that approves the result, so it was throwing away landings it would have been happy with. It now tries progressively shorter pieces of the wording, and copes with the invisible spacing characters some sites put between words. A piece is only used when it appears exactly once on the page, so a teaser box that repeats the story's opening line cannot capture the landing.

Magazine-style posts land on the story instead of the summary line. A layout that runs headline, then a one-line summary, then the author and date and "6 min read", then the article, used to land you on the summary line. The tell is where the author block sits: a summary comes above it, the story below. The add-on now reads past the summary to the first real paragraph. Stories that open with one short sentence and no author block, like MacRumors, still land on that sentence.

Diagnostic logging stays off unless you switch it on. The add-on can keep a technical log to help track down a page that lands badly, and it writes nothing at all unless you ask for it. To turn it on, create an empty file named TextMarksTheSpot-diagnostics-enabled in your NVDA user configuration folder and restart NVDA. To turn it back off, delete that file.

Tested with NVDA 2026.2. Nothing needed changing for it. The add-on still runs on NVDA 2024.1 and newer, on both the 32-bit builds up to 2025.3 and the 64-bit builds from 2026.1 on.

New: the buffer window. Press NVDA+Enter in a terminal to open the whole scrollback as a browsable snapshot: arrow through it, press H to move between the commands you ran and the errors they produced, follow the table of contents, read columnar output as real tables, and activate web links. NVDA+Shift+Enter opens a jump to line dialog that moves the review cursor to any line, found by its text. In the command layer, Shift+E shows only errors and Shift+C only the commands you ran.

Also new: any terminal NVDA recognizes is supported, not just those on a built-in list, so terminals the add-on used to ignore now work. Find reaches the scrollback on the legacy Windows console, where NVDA can only read the visible screen. And there is an optional word echo for terminals.

Fixed: braille follows the cursor again. Typing did not update the display until you panned away and back, and it never jumped back to the cursor. Key echo also no longer requires turning NVDA's own typing settings off; inside terminals it replaces them.

Security: passwords are no longer spoken by key echo. Characters are masked and completed words are never spoken while the terminal marks input as protected.

Laptop keyboard layout: NVDA+Enter is NVDA's activate-navigator-object command; Terminal Access takes it only inside terminals. Use the command layer's Enter, or reassign in Input Gestures, if you need NVDA's command there.

* Fixed several settings not taking effect, so the add-on now uses the options you choose rather than its default values.
* Added an option to read only subtitles in one language, for videos that mix languages. Type a language code such as ar, en or ja and tick "Read only subtitles in this language" to skip logos and credits written in another one.
* Fixed a subtitle losing one of its lines when both lines looked alike.
* Fixed a line being skipped when recognition briefly missed it.
* Added a "Restore default settings" button to the settings panel.
* Added an optional detailed diagnostic log, off by default, for use when reporting a problem.
* Improved the filter for text in capital letters: it now uses the subtitle language code to tell a cast name from a sentence, so longer credit lines are skipped while capitalised dialogue is kept.
* Fixed a subtitle being read again each time text beside it changed, such as rolling credits recognised as part of the subtitle line.
* Fixed the filters removing ordinary dialogue and short words, and removing subtitles written in some languages.

Commander. 
It makes navigating files and folders easier — especially for braille display users.
Braille display:
- A letter at the beginning of each line shows which panel you are in (for example the left or right file panel).
- The letter is lowercase when an item is not selected, and UPPERCASE when it is selected.
- At the end of each line you see your position in the list, for example 3/42.
Speech:
- NVDA announces your position in the list naturally, for example "3 of 42".
- Speech and braille output are independent of each other — the prefix letter is shown on the braille display only and is never spoken.
General:
- Column separators in file names are displayed as spaces, so lines are easier to read.

* Skip blank lines during text scrolling.
* Speech History Mode.

Main features include:
* Reload two favorite braille displays with shortcuts

* Multiple input and output braille tables, with automatic table selection on NVDA 2025.1 and later

* Optional second Liblouis pass after the main output table

* Speak the current line while scrolling (coordinate with NVDA braille speech settings)
* Convert text to Unicode braille and back, and between Unicode braille and dot-number descriptions
* Lock the braille keyboard; lock modifier keys from the braille display
* Quick launches to applications or web addresses; table dictionaries
* One-handed braille input; rules for undefined characters including emoji; advanced input mode and abbreviations
* Speech History Mode; configurable rotor; object and document presentation options for braille; role labels; routing in edit fields; margins; updates; and other settings

Where a display profile exists, the add-on can add extended gesture maps (function keys, multimedia keys, rotor actions, emulated modifiers, and more). Fixed chords being flattened. When two keys overlapped, the release of the first was injected in the same
system call as the press of the second, so the two were never held down at the same moment and the target
application saw two unrelated keystrokes instead of the combination. Presses now only ever travel with
presses and releases with releases.
Raising the playback speed no longer shrinks the overlap between two keys to nothing; keys held together
now stay together for at least the configured minimum hold time.

1.0

First release of Macro Studio.

Macro Studio continues the work of NVDA Macro Manager by Muhammet Enes Şenovalı as a separate add-on, so that
development can carry on actively. The keyboard engine of the original add-on was rewritten and a large number
of defects were fixed before this release.

Playback engine:
Keys that were pressed together are now replayed together. A whole chord is injected with a single system call
instead of one key after another, and overlapping or held keys keep their original order and timing.
Keys chosen from the key list now carry their real scan code and extended flag, so arrows, Insert, Delete,
Home, End, right Ctrl, right Alt and numpad divide no longer arrive as a different key.
Fixed the key list replacing standard letters with layout specific keys, which could send a completely
different key than the one selected.
Fixed partially rejected keystroke batches being resent in full, which produced duplicate keystrokes.
Fixed a race that allowed the same macro to start twice and interleave its keystrokes.
Fixed a hold time floor that was applied to every key release and pulled apart keys released together.
Fixed the application lock being bypassed when the foreground application could not be identified.

Recording:
Fixed a recording that repeated a single key being erased by the stop hotkey trimming.
Fixed key events that are not real key transitions being stored and then silently dropped on playback.
Recording can no longer be started while a macro is playing, and a failed keyboard hook is now reported.

Macros and interface:
Fixed macros saved from the dialog being locked to NVDA itself instead of the target application.
Fixed the smart loop optimiser dropping most repetitions of macros with a loop count above one.
Fixed duplicated macros sharing an identifier, which made one of them impossible to assign a gesture to.
Fixed the macro list keeping a hidden extra selection, so deleting could remove the wrong macro.
Fixed hold-to-run, which failed on every hotkey and could stop itself on its own keystrokes.
Fixed an empty playback speed field aborting the save.
Fixed all playback messages failing silently because a loop variable shadowed the translation function.
Export file names are now sanitised and the clipboard import is size limited.
The dark dialog colours are only applied when Windows itself is in dark mode.
Keyboard hooks are released when the add-on is unloaded.

- Removed VLC / PotPlayer / Windows Media Player fallback support. BASS is
now the sole, mandatory playback backend. This removes the "Disable BASS
backend" option and its VLC/wmplayer/PotPlayer path settings from the
FreeRadio settings panel; if BASS itself fails to start, playback now
fails with a clear error instead of silently switching to another
player.
- Internal cleanup: removed unused code paths and a dead
"player_paths" field from scheduled recordings that was never actually
used for playback.
- **Seeking within a podcast or audio book now supports tap-to-jump amounts:** a single press seeks 12 seconds, two quick presses seek 1 minute, three quick presses seek 5 minutes. Holding the key down still seeks continuously in the original 5-second steps, unchanged.
**Improved**
- Station search now also matches on **codec**, **bitrate**, and **language**, in addition to name, country, and tags. For example, searching "aac" or "320" now finds stations using that codec or bitrate, and results can be combined with other terms (e.g. "jazz 320"). Partialy closing #30
Add a new source for audio books
- Added LibriVox as a second audio book source alongside GETEM. Both catalogs now share the same Audio Books tab: search, browse, play, and resume progress work the same way regardless of which source a book came from.
- Searching the Audio Books tab now queries GETEM and LibriVox together, and results from both are combined into a single list.
- Pasting a LibriVox or Getem book URL directly into the search field now resolves and adds that book.
- Added an "Audio book sources" option to the settings panel: a checkbox list lets you choose which of GETEM and LibriVox are searched (both are enabled by default).
- **GETEM catalog & detail-page parsing: replaced regex scraping with a real DOM parser**
The HTML-scraping code that read GETEM's search results and work-detail pages relied on regexes over raw HTML and a literal string split to find each result row. That approach breaks silently the moment the site changes something cosmetic — element order, an extra wrapper tag, a label nested one level deeper — without changing what the page actually means.
Replaced it with a small, dependency-free DOM builder on top of Python's standard `html.parser.HTMLParser`, then rewrote every scraping function to query that tree by tag/class instead of matching raw markup:
- **Catalog search results**: each result row is now parsed as its own real subtree, so a field missing from one row can no longer leak text belonging to the next row — a risk the old row-splitting approach carried.
- **Format-filter options, hidden form fields**: read directly from parsed `<select>`/`<option>` elements instead of locating them by substring search.
- **Work-detail pages**: chapter links, title, and metadata fields (author/narrator/publisher/etc.) are now found by walking the tree rather than requiring an exact tag sequence; a field's own label text is excluded via nesting-depth-independent lookup instead of an assumed fixed `</div></div>` boundary.
- **URL resolution**: relative/absolute link handling now goes through `urllib.parse.urljoin`, which correctly covers protocol-relative and query-only links the old hand-written checks didn't.
- No public function signatures changed, so nothing else in the add-on needed touching. Verified against hand-built fixtures covering the exact failure modes the old code was vulnerable to (reordered attributes, div/span markup variance, a field missing mid-listing, a link wrapped in an extra tag, a deeply nested label) — all resolved correctly.

*   **Recent Documents in the Reader**: Pressing **D** in the Command Layer now shows your recently read documents first. Pick one to continue from the page you were on — even when the OCR already finished — or press **Open File...** (`Ctrl + O`) to browse as usual.
*   **Push to Talk for Live Assistant**: Take full control of your live conversations! Enable **Push to Talk** in the new Live Assistant settings tab and assign any key — or even a lone modifier like `Left Ctrl` — to talk. Hold the key to speak and release it when you're done, with a short beep on each press and release. *   **Settings Backup & Restore**: Added a powerful backup and restore system in the **Advanced** tab! You can now save all of your add-on settings — including API keys, models, custom prompts, and preferences — into a single JSON file, and restore them perfectly at any time, on any machine, or after reinstalling NVDA. When backing up, you choose what to include: **Everything** (settings, custom labels, OCR progress, and history) or **Settings Only**.
*   **Direct Text & HTML Reading**: The Document Reader can now open plain text (`.txt`) and HTML (`.html`, `.htm`) files directly! It automatically detects the file encoding, strips scripts and formatting clutter, and intelligently splits the content into readable pages — even re-importing its own exported files while preserving page structure — so you can read them instantly with no OCR or AI processing!
*   **Gemini Live TTS for the Document Reader**: The "Generate Audio" button now supports Gemini Live — a high-quality, natural-pace streaming text-to-speech engine! When Gemini is your active provider, you can choose between Standard TTS and Gemini Live right in the reader, and your selection is remembered for next time!
*   **Custom Prompt Shortcuts**: You can now assign a shortcut key to any of your custom prompts right from the Prompt Manager! Give every prompt its own dedicated key or key combination to run it instantly, automatically capturing your current selection or context with zero extra steps!
*   **Chat Message Navigation**: Review any conversation hands-free! Inside any chat window (Direct Chat, document chat, refine, and more), press `Alt + Down` to hear the next message and `Alt + Up` to hear the previous one — with clear "You" / "AI" prefixes and "First message" / "Last message" boundaries announced as you go.
*   **Copy Chat Message (Alt + C)**: While reviewing a conversation with `Alt + Up/Down`, press `Alt + C` to copy the message you are currently on to the clipboard — respecting your Clean Markdown setting — with a spoken confirmation.
*   **Direct Chat System Prompt**: The Direct Chat (`Shift+C`) now has its own editable system prompt — "Direct Chat Instruction" — that sets the assistant's persona and response language for every conversation. You can customize it from the Prompt Manager's Default Prompts tab.
*   **Document Reader Cursor Page Navigation**: Reading multi-page documents just got smoother! In the Document Viewer, when your cursor reaches the last line of a page and you press `Down`, the reader automatically jumps to the next page. Pressing `Up` at the start of a page seamlessly takes you back to the previous one — no more manual page switching while reading!
*   **New Quick Settings Toggles**: Copy AI responses to clipboard, Direct Output (no chat window), Clean Markdown in Chat, and Smart Swap can now be switched on and off instantly from the command layer's Quick Settings!
*   **Live Assistant Settings Tab**: The Live Assistant now has its own dedicated settings tab! The "Live Assistant: Direct Output (No Window)" option moved here from the Connection tab, and the tab appears only when Google Gemini (or a Gemini-compatible Custom provider) is your active provider.

YouTube Access Pro is an NVDA add-on that provides full keyboard-only access to YouTube. Search or paste a link to play and download videos, playlists, or channels directly, with complete playback shortcuts (play/pause, seek, volume, speed, automatic continuous playback) and a built-in sleep timer.

Manage personal playlists freely, and follow favorite channels through the Subscriptions tab, browsing content the way YouTube itself organizes it - Videos, Shorts, Live, and Playlists. Download instantly as MP3 or MP4 with selectable quality, automatically sorted into folders by playlist or channel.

Available in both Thai and English, switch instantly with Ctrl+T. Open the window from anywhere with NVDA+Y, and hear a shortcut summary for the current tab anytime with Ctrl+F1. A full user guide with complete shortcut details is included with this add-on.

2026.09.02: Confirmed compatibility with NVDA 2026.2 (released 2026-08-31) and updated lastTestedNVDAVersion accordingly. Reviewed NVDA 2026.2's developer changelog (new Magnifier, touch gestures, speech dictionaries, braille auto-scroll, deprecated speechDictHandler constants) and confirmed none of it affects this add-on's code, since this add-on does not use any of those APIs - no functional code changes were needed.
2026.08.25: Fixed MP4 downloads failing outright while MP3 downloads kept working normally. The MP4 download format selector only matched a video that YouTube had already muxed together with its audio into one file - YouTube increasingly does not offer such a combined format at all for many videos anymore, so the download matched nothing and failed. MP4 downloads now request the best available video and audio streams separately and mux them together with the bundled ffmpeg (same as this add-on already does for live playback and MP3 extraction), which works regardless of whether YouTube offers a combined format for a given video.
2026.08.20: Fixed the automatic yt-dlp update checker only checking once every 24 hours, which made it easy to reasonably believe automatic updates were not working at all - it now checks on every NVDA startup instead (still only if enabled in Settings). Added a self-check that runs after a real restart to verify a yt-dlp update that reported success actually took effect, and warns you plainly if it did not (most likely causes: antivirus/Windows Defender blocking the newly-written files, or another NVDA installation on this computer) instead of silently staying on the old version with no explanation. Updated the bundled yt-dlp library to the latest stable release (2026.08.19).
2026.08.18: Updated the bundled yt-dlp library (2026.07.04 to a 2026.08.17 pre-release build) to fix YouTube extraction breaking for pasted links ("Could not fetch data") - YouTube had changed something extraction-dependent since the previous release, and yt-dlp's maintainers had already shipped several fix builds ahead of their next stable release. Currently-live broadcasts now open directly in the user's default browser instead of playing inside the add-on, since the browser's own native YouTube player handles live playback more reliably than the bundled offline media player ever could. Added a "Live" search type alongside Video/Playlist/Channel, to find currently-live broadcasts by keyword directly from the Search and Download tab (previously only reachable per-channel via the Subscriptions tab's Live section). Also fixes an unrelated ordinary-video playback bug where mpv's own internal link resolver was incorrectly re-engaging on links this add-on had already resolved itself, occasionally cutting playback short before the end.
2026.07.19: Full-featured release. Search, play, and download YouTube videos, playlists, and channels entirely by keyboard - audio playback with full transport control (play/pause, seek, volume, speed, previous/next with automatic continue), a sleep timer, personal playlist management, and a Subscriptions tab that browses a followed channel's Videos, Shorts, Live, and Playlists the way YouTube itself organizes them. Download to MP3 or MP4 with selectable quality, auto-sorted into folders by playlist or channel name. Full English/Thai interface with instant switching (Control+T).

This add-on (Virtual Notes for NVDA) creates virtual notes that can be read by NVDA screen reader. Notes are persistent and saved automatically to disk.

For more information, tutorials, and updates, visit:
* Official Website: https://julianolopes.com.br/complemento-notas-virtuais-para-o-nvda
* Demonstration Video on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=yKJqS4imKHg

Here are the available shortcuts:  
* NVDA + Alt + A: Add selected text to memory as a new note. If no text is selected, it opens a dialog for manual entry, where you can use buttons to:
  * Create a new note.
  * Replace the current note.
  * Add the typed text to the beginning of the current note.
  * Insert the typed text right after the current line of the active note.
  * Add the typed text to the end of the current note.
  * Rename a voice note (if the active note is an audio note).
* NVDA + Alt + V: Add a new note directly from the clipboard.
* NVDA + Shift + Alt + A: Insert selected text as a new line right after the current line in the active note.
* NVDA + Alt + J: Go to the previous note.
* NVDA + Alt + L: Go to the next note.
* NVDA + Alt + U: Announce/play the current note.
* NVDA + CONTROL + SHIFT + U: Paste the current note to the current application.
* NVDA + Alt + S: Replace the note in the current position (you need to select some text first).
* NVDA + Alt + D: Delete the note in the current position.
* NVDA + Alt + G: Record a voice note (16-bit 44.1 kHz Mono). Press again to stop recording.
* NVDA + Shift + Alt + U: Pause or resume recording or playback of the current voice note.

If the current note contains multiple lines (like text copied from a text editor), you can use these shortcuts:  
* NVDA + Alt + I: Move to the previous line of the current note.
* NVDA + Alt + K: Move to the next line of the current note.
* NVDA + Alt + O: Announce the current line of the current note.
* NVDA + CONTROL + SHIFT + O: Paste the current line in the note to the current application.

Note: The key positions mimic the arrow keys (I = up, L = right, K = down, and J = left).  
After using a shortcut, a specific sound will play to indicate the action performed.

you are working in. No window opens and focus never moves: the notes are loaded into memory and you browse them entirely with keyboard gestures, while the app you are in keeps the focus.

Folders and notes:
- NVDA+ALT+P: open the current folder in File Explorer
- NVDA+ALT+[: previous folder
- NVDA+ALT+]: next folder
- NVDA+ALT+N: load the notes in the current folder
- NVDA+ALT+U: previous note
- NVDA+ALT+O: next note

Reading:
- NVDA+ALT+SHIFT+A: read the whole note
- NVDA+ALT+I: previous line
- NVDA+ALT+K: next line
- NVDA+ALT+J: previous word
- NVDA+ALT+L: next word
- NVDA+ALT+,: previous character
- NVDA+ALT+.: next character
- NVDA+ALT+H: start of line
- NVDA+ALT+': end of line
- NVDA+ALT+Space: render the note as Markdown and read it in a browse-mode window

Copying:
- NVDA+ALT+A: copy the whole note
- NVDA+ALT+;: copy the current line
- NVDA+ALT+F9: set the selection start at the current position
- NVDA+ALT+F10: set the selection end; press twice to copy the selection
- NVDA+ALT+BACKSPACE: clear the selection markers

Encoding:
- NVDA+ALT+E: switch to the next note encoding
- NVDA+ALT+SHIFT+E: switch to the previous note encoding

Settings live in NVDA's Settings dialog (NVDA+CTRL+S) under the Invisinote category. An Open Invisinote settings command that jumps straight to that category is available in NVDA's Input Gestures dialog, under the invisinote category, if you would like to assign a shortcut of your own.

    Version 2.2.0:
    - Gemini and Hugging Face are now tried first for higher-quality, more
      reliable results; the free g4f backend is off by default since it
      relies on unofficial access to third-party services and can break
      without notice (can be re-enabled in settings)
    - Fixed: generated text no longer permanently overwrites your clipboard -
      your previous clipboard contents are restored after every paste
    - Fixed: all shortcuts are now guarded against being triggered twice at
      once (e.g. pressing NVDA+Shift+H repeatedly while busy)
    - Fixed: language auto-detection now matches whole words only, so
      instructions like "German engineering" no longer force German output
    - Fixed: error messages are now short and screen-reader friendly instead
      of raw technical text
    - Added: NVDA+Shift+X to cancel a generation in progress
    - Added: NVDA+Shift+R to regenerate the last action
    - Added: NVDA+Shift+Y to browse recent generation history
    - Added: spoken preview of generated text (toggle in settings)
    - Added: periodic progress tone during slow requests so NVDA doesn't
      feel frozen
    - Added: provider indicator shown with translation/refine/history results
    - Added: tone and length can now be set inline in your instructions
      (e.g. "a short, friendly email about...") in addition to language
    - Added: editable per-content-type prompt templates in settings
    - Added: settings now disclose that API keys are stored locally in
      plain text

    Version 2.1.0:
    - Added Content Type selection (Email, Story, Blog, Message, Social, Poem, Essay, Report)
    - NVDA+Shift+G: Generate title for any topic
    - NVDA+Shift+H: Generate full content (stories, blogs, emails, etc.)

Commander. 
It makes navigating files and folders easier — especially for braille display users.
Braille display:
- A letter at the beginning of each line shows which panel you are in (for example the left or right file panel).
- The letter is lowercase when an item is not selected, and UPPERCASE when it is selected.
- At the end of each line you see your position in the list, for example 3/42.
Speech:
- NVDA announces your position in the list naturally, for example "3 of 42".
- Speech and braille output are independent of each other — the prefix letter is shown on the braille display only and is never spoken.
General:
- Column separators in file names are displayed as spaces, so lines are easier to read.

- Pins the official Pandoc 3.1.11.1 binary for local reference and CI
  documentation builds. CI verifies the archive by SHA-256, while the build
  script rejects differently packaged builds of the same version so they
  cannot generate different checked-in installed HTML.
- Assigns `NVDA+Alt+N` to the contextual activation command by default. The
  gesture remains reassignable in NVDA's Input Gestures dialog and continues
  to pass through outside a matching focused Windows Terminal control.
- Makes Neovim's built-in `:Tutor` specifically more accessible without adding
  separate tutorial logic. From Neovim 0.12, recognized, unambiguous native
  Tutor extmarks provide localized announcements when an assessment changes,
  the assessment when its line is read again, and persistent non-routable
  Braille markers. Other buffers and extmarks remain untouched. Invalid
  transitions, including structurally invalid JSON values, are rejected before
  canonical state, while
  existing Braille routing and source mappings are preserved. On Neovim 0.10
  the Tutor path is fully inactive and registers no observers. Transition
  announcements remain bound to the same buffer, window, and line context.
  Isolated headless boundary tests and a real 0.12.3
  TUI contract test cover the scope; the Tutor was also sampled practically
  under Windows/NVDA with speech and a physical Braille display.
- Restores NVDA's normal terminal behavior immediately after a remote Neovim
  instance exits. The SSH client now treats the authenticated bridge
  `disconnected` state as connection lifecycle rather than an ordinary editor
  event, even while SSH and the bridge remain alive. Invalid state values are
  rejected, and a later reconnect again requires a valid `fullState`.
- Adds a component-dialog configuration choice that remains unchanged by
  default and can install a basic configuration with Lazy, Oil, the bundled
  Access Link copy, actual tab characters on two-column tab stops, disabled
  line numbers, and leader commands for Oil and Lazy. The indentation
  remains fixed after filetype-specific Neovim defaults are applied. An
  isolated headless startup with local Access Link, Lazy, and Oil directories
  is checked under Neovim 0.10.1.
  Existing regular `init.lua` and `init.vim` files move to unique backup paths
  named in the results dialog before atomic replacement; failures restore the
  originals from the retained backups. Symbolic links and unusual targets
  remain unchanged, and component removal deletes neither configuration nor
  backups. The local Windows basic configuration has practical acceptance.
- Adds a second configuration path that safely copies the complete local
  Windows configuration directory to selected Linux connections. A bounded,
  link-free snapshot is transferred separately from the component package over
  SSH and validated again on the target; existing configurations are backed up
  as complete directories before atomic replacement. Windows-specific content
  and execute permissions are neither guessed nor rewritten. Lazy must still
  list the installed Access Link copy explicitly as a local plugin.
- Hardens component removal with an explicit warning that defaults to
  declining and a repeated results notice. The plugin and Linux bridge are
  removed; Neovim configuration and backups remain unchanged, including any
  explicit plugin load instruction that the user must remove when appropriate.
- Adds robust baseline support for `lazy.nvim`: Access Link gives the real
  Lazy buffer an unambiguous context name and speaks the complete command bar
  regardless of its initial blank line or width-dependent wrapping. Line
  navigation omits visual-only edge and padding spaces. Graphical private-use
  Unicode characters remain silent throughout the Lazy buffer, including
  speech exploration, while Braille retains the unmodified text. Only documented
  lifecycle events produce neutral start/end reports through speech and
  Braille. Plugin rows identified unambiguously through public icon highlights
  report NVDA's localized `collapsed` or `expanded` state when entered or
  toggled; Braille shows the corresponding tree-view markers `+` and `-`.
  Toggling does not obscure them with a transient Braille message, and existing
  NVDA line exploration reads the command bar again when needed. Unclear
  rendering remains silent. Synchronization collapses child operations
  without guessing progress, result, or success from Lazy's rendering.
- Adds four guided lazy.nvim practical tests for window operation, install,
  update, and synchronization. Isolated local Git fixtures and pinned headless
  contract tests verify actual end states without changing user configuration
  or installed plugins. The individual selector lists these tasks under
  plugin management. Technical preflight accounts for Lazy deliberately not
  opening its UI in headless mode; local fixture repositories run without
  line-ending conversion or distracting Git progress output.
  The F5 final-state check treats an empty optional path list consistently as
  an array instead of Lua `vim.NIL` and names the revisions and removals it
  actually confirmed. All four guided workflows were practically confirmed in
  the Windows/NVDA reference path; their completion reports remain explicitly
  neutral until F5 proves the Git end state.
- Integrates all eight German and English HTML documents into the add-on. A
  top-level `Neovim Access Link` menu opens settings, component management,
  and installed help selected for NVDA's language.
- Documents the separate, assignable commands for copying a Visual selection
  or register 0 to the Windows clipboard and inserting Windows clipboard text
  into Neovim.
- Adds the default help file and a change log generated from the current
  German or English changelog section to the manifest.
  Development builds use the unreleased section; releases curate it into the
  version section and then reset it.
- Strictly validates built base and localization manifests against the official
  NVDA AddonTemplate field set. Missing, empty, unknown, or malformed metadata
  and missing default English help stop the package build.

0.97.0

- Adds the HTTPS project URL to the add-on manifest.
- Adds an optional parameterless Windows build from source. A temporary Python
  environment leaves the system installation unchanged, while the embedded
  Linux package receives portable Python modules and reproducible Unix
  metadata.
- Adds Insert-mode LSP active-parameter speech and held, read-only signature,
  parameter, and diagnostic views with correlated speech and Braille.
- Hardens native completion, `nvim-cmp`, and `blink.cmp`, including
  documentation resolution, menu cues, and the no-selected-candidate state.
  It also fixes the practical-test preflight incorrectly rejecting Blink's
  intentionally disabled automatic menu display.
- Makes native incremental search, `inccommand` replacement previews, Quickfix
  and location lists, replacement prompts, multi-buffer replacement, and LSP
  rename completion accessible. Neovim and the language server retain
  execution; Access Link coalesces internal buffer, cursor, and context changes
  into one evidence-based completion report. Automated multi-file tests cover
  Quickfix files, listed buffers, and argument files; guided L4 through L6
  isolate the remaining practical NVDA checks.
- Unifies diagnostics from LSP, `nvim-lint`, ALE, and `none-ls.nvim`, extends
  navigation commands, and adds distinct error, warning, and empty-result
  cues. On Windows, the Clang-Tidy practical test launches the pinned binary
  directly, uses an explicit C mode and supplied test configuration, and
  consumes both output streams. One bounded wait allowance accommodates cold
  provider starts on Windows and network drives.
  Markdownlint checks the absolute fixture instead of relying on an unreliable
  cold stdin run. Setup probes real linter output first and collects failures
  from all selected profiles in one run.
- Fixes Linux session discovery across differing runtime environments and
  without `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR`, plus focus and remembered-binding paths after the
  optional F12 question.
- Separates safe, SSH, and socket verification into independent test phases
  and expands reproducible completion, LSP, linter, and guided practical tests.
  Compact task cards state purpose, numbered steps, and pass condition; F2
  repeats the task while F1 and F11 remain free because of Neovim and Windows
  Terminal default bindings.
- Updates selection and LSP test APIs for Neovim 0.12 while retaining Neovim
  0.10 compatibility.
- Restructures the Quick Guide and manual around reader tasks. One real,
  tested Lua example generates identical code blocks for GitHub and the German
  and English HTML manuals.
- Clarifies the Global Plugin's remaining process-wide role after a renewed
  architecture audit without broadening the AppModule-owned event path.
- Reorganizes developer documentation around onboarding, current explanation,
  tasks, references, and decisions; removes stale transport claims and adds a
  dedicated CI build with automated German/English structure and HTML metadata

= 2026.09.09 =
- Initial release.
- Speaks automatically as soon as NVDA finishes starting, with no key press required.
- Default greeting is time-of-day aware (good morning, afternoon, or evening).
- Add your own custom messages instead of the default greeting; if you add more than one, a different one is spoken each time NVDA starts.
- Adds an "NVDA Startup Greeter" category to NVDA Settings to enable/disable the greeting or manage your custom messages.
- Also shows a matching message on a connected braille display.

The following features, deriving from Braille Extender, are available:

* Reload two favorite braille display with shortcuts.
* Automatic review cursor tethering in terminal role like in PuTTY, Powershell, bash, cmd.
* Auto scroll.
* Switch between several input/output braille tables.
* Mark the text with special attributes through dot 7, dot 8 or both.
* Use two output braille tables simultaneously.
* Display tab signs as spaces.
* Reverse forward scroll and back scroll buttons.
* Say the current line during text scrolling either in review mode, or in focus mode or both.
* Translate text easily in Unicode braille and vice versa. E.g.: z <--> ⠵.
* Convert cell description to Unicode braille and vice versa. E.g.: 123 <--> ⠇.
* Lock braille keyboard.
* Launch an application/URL with gesture.
* Braille dictionaries.
* Type with one-hand from braille keyboard.
* Display undefined characters from braille tables (including emojis) using altenative representations.
* Enter any character from braille keyboard (including emojis).
* Skip blank lines during text scrolling.
* Speech History Mode.

And much more.

For some braille displays, it extends the braille display commands to provide:

* Offer complete gesture maps including function keys, multimedia keys, quick navigation, etc.

* Speech History Mode; configurable rotor; object and document presentation options for braille; role labels; routing in edit fields; margins; updates; and other settings
